dedupe_keys.name: a large scale dataset for training deep learning segmentation and tracking of extreme weather

description: A large-scale dataset for training deep learning segmentation and tracking of extreme weather is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Sol Kim et al. As Earth’s climate continues to undergo changes, it is imperative to gain understanding of how high-impact, extreme weather events will change. Researchers are increasingly relying on data-driven, learning-based approaches for the detection and tracking of extreme weather events. Coverage: not stated; published in 2025. Formats: ZIP, NetCDF. The data are held in Harvard Dataverse and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 197127997. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC0-1.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked, and the coverage and resolution are those of the abstract only. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
